html:
Daphni is a Byzantine monastery about 11 kilometres northwest of Athens, on the old Sacred Way to Eleusis. Its church, built around 1080 to 1100, holds some of the finest mosaics of the late 11th century.

The name means "laurel grove", after the laurels of an ancient sanctuary of Apollo that once stood nearby. The mosaics show the lives of Christ and the Virgin on a gold ground, with graceful, classical figures. The most famous is the stern Christ Pantokrator, "ruler of all", gazing down from the dome.

After the Fourth Crusade the monastery passed to Cistercian monks from Burgundy under the Frankish rulers of the Duchy of Athens, some of whom were buried there. It suffered in later wars and earthquakes, most recently in 1999. With Hosios Loukas and Nea Moni on Chios, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a key example of the art of the Byzantine Empire.
